title: Progressive cross-encoder -> bi-encoder onboarding and delta profile publication
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a repeatable pipeline to onboard cross-encoder rerankers and produce compact bi-encoder variants for high-throughput embedding/rerank use-cases. The goal is to support progressive onboarding where:
  1) a cross-encoder is profiled under full-latency evaluation;
  2) an automated distillation-to-bi-encoder (or asymmetric pair encoder) produces candidate low-latency variants;
  3) we generate delta performance profiles (relative to the canonical profile) and publish only the deltas to the catalog to reduce profile churn.

Motivation / Rationale:
Many customers prefer cross-encoders for top-quality reranking but need bi-encoder fallbacks for scale and cost. Current onboarding creates full independent profiles for every distilled variant, which bloats the catalog and slows review. Publishing delta profiles (what changed vs the pinned canonical cross-encoder) should reduce reviewers' cognitive load and make rollouts faster while retaining traceability for regressions.

Scope / Deliverables:
- Data pipeline that can run cross-encoder evaluation (accuracy, nDCG, latency distribution) and trigger distillation runs producing 3 candidate bi-encoders (fast/medium/compact).
- Automated delta profiler that computes and stores differences in metrics and configuration (quantization, tokenization changes, sequence length assumptions).
- A delta-first publishing flow in the profile registry UI and API so reviewers see changes as a compact diff and can approve/rollback.
- Canary harness to run hybrid traffic (10% cross-encoder, 90% bi-encoder) and gather production delta metrics for 48h before final pin.
- Tests and e2e checks to ensure that published delta profiles are reversible and reconstitute the full profile for legacy consumers.

Progress updates (chronological):
- 2025-11-12: Ticket created (Asha). Initial design doc linked below and spike accepted.
- 2025-11-18: Spike completed. Found that current profile schema lacks explicit "variant_parent" and "delta_bucket" fields; proposed schema extension in Confluence.
- 2025-11-24: Implementation spike for distillation orchestration started. P0 blocker: GPU quotas for distill jobs on staging; raised to infra (ENG-50090).
- 2025-11-30: First automated delta generator (metrics-only) committed (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-pipeline/pull/1543). Unit tests green.
- 2025-12-03: UX sync with PM/Design. Decision: delta view must present both metric diffs and config diffs side-by-side; design mock in Drive.
- 2025-12-05: Canary harness prototype deployed to dedicated cluster; running 24h smoke. Early signal: bi-encoder compact variant shows 12x throughput increase and -3.4% nDCG for top-10 on internal corpus.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Publish deltas instead of full profiles to reduce storage and reviewer noise. Trade-off: consumers must support on-the-fly profile reconstruction; we mitigate by providing server-side reconstruction API and one-click full-profile export.
- Perform production canary with 48h minimum; this increases time-to-pin but reduces regression risk.
- Keep delta schema minimal (metrics, config keys touched, recommended routing logic) to avoid compatibility issues with older console versions.

Review feedback and action items:
- PM (Lena Ortiz): request to include monitoring thresholds for "acceptable delta" (default: nDCG drop <= 1.5% and latency <= 2x). Added to acceptance criteria.
- Design (Ravi Shah): requested inline evidence links (evaluation notebooks) in delta UI. Action: add attachments list to profile registry API.
- Security (Maya Lin): confirm that distillation artifacts do not leak training data. Action: add synthetic workload audit to e2e tests.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Distillation introduces unobserved failure modes (semantic shifts). Mitigation: require automated slice-level checks and human review for any delta with accuracy degradation > 0.5%.
- Risk: Registry consumers that cannot reconstruct full profiles. Mitigation: provide server-side reconstruction and backward compatibility flag in API.

Acceptance criteria:
- Pipeline can autonomously generate bi-encoder candidate models and produce delta profiles for at least 3 test cross-encoder models.
- Delta profile publishes show a clear metrics diff in the registry UI and API with evidence links.
- Canary harness runs for 48h and produces a pass/fail signal consistent with offline evaluation >90% of the time on our internal corpora.
- Rollout pin action attaches delta metadata and can be rolled back within 1 hour with no data loss.

Next steps (owner -> date):
- Marco: finish profile-reconstruction API and publish OpenAPI spec (2025-12-10).
- ML infra: clear GPU quota for distill jobs on staging (ENG-50090) (2025-12-07).
- Design: deliver delta UI mock and attach to PR (2025-12-08).
- QA: create e2e synthetic audit harness and test plan (2025-12-12).

- Design notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ML/Delta+Profiles+Design

- Canary dashboard (staging): https://dash.redwood.ai/r/cluster/canary-459

Notes for reviewers:
Look for the delta schema changes in the Confluence doc and the PRs. Focus reviews on the reconstruction API contract and canary rollback safety. If we approve the delta flow, we can cut the profile review time by an estimated 40% for distilled variants.
